cohort: 1213 women with low-risk singleton pregnancies at 41 to 42 weeks of gestation undergoing induction of labor
finding: Induction of labor with oral misoprostol, compared to a transvaginal balloon catheter, resulted in a lower likelihood of vaginal delivery within 24 hours and a longer duration until vaginal delivery, although safety outcomes and childbirth experience were similar between the two groups.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery (non-operative vaginal delivery and cesarean delivery rates) did not differ between induction of labor with oral misoprostol compared with a transvaginal balloon catheter.
